title: Apple Built a Separate AI for China
hook: Reuters reports Apple trained a China-only model with Alibaba's help. The AI on your phone isn't one global product — it's whatever your country's rules allow.
key_points: The Verge, citing Reuters, reports Apple trained a China-specific LLM with Alibaba.
The partnership is notable for crossing US-China tech tensions rather than avoiding them.
Operating in China means a domestic partner and compliance with local content rules.
The practical upshot: the same app can give different answers in different countries.
Where a model was trained and by whose rules is part of what it will and won't say.
content_html: Apple has trained a custom large language model for the Chinese market in partnership with Alibaba, The Verge reports, citing a Reuters account based on people familiar with the work. It's an unusual cross-border collaboration at a moment when US and Chinese tech interests are pulling apart.
extra_html: The business logic is straightforward: to sell AI features in China, a foreign company generally needs a domestic partner and a model that complies with local content rules. The idea worth carrying away is less about Apple than about AI in general. We tend to imagine a model as a single object with fixed knowledge, but it's a product shaped by whoever built it and whichever regulator has jurisdiction. Two people opening the same assistant in two countries can get materially different answers — not because one of them is broken, but because they aren't running the same model at all.

related.title: Who Controls AI?
related.hook: The most powerful AI models are built by a handful of giant companies, because training them costs a fortune. Who holds that power — and whether 'open' AI can balance it — shapes everything.

related.title: China's Free-to-Download Models Are Closing the Gap
related.hook: A Chinese lab's openly downloadable model reportedly rivals the top US models at some security tasks — a sign the distance between open AI and the frontier is shrinking fast.

related.title: Can Cloud AI Be Private? Apple's Bet
related.hook: Apple's pitch for its AI is privacy: small models run on your device, and bigger ones run in the cloud — even on Google's servers — in a way Apple says gives the host no access to your data.

flashcards.prompt: Why would Apple train a separate model just for the China market?

choices.text: Operating there requires a domestic partner and compliance with local rules
Chinese phones use a different kind of processor for text
Apple's global model works only in English

flashcards.explanation_html: A market-specific model with a local partner is how a foreign company meets China's regulatory and content requirements.

flashcards.prompt: What does a region-specific model mean for you as a user?
flashcards.back_html: The same app can answer differently depending on where you are. What a model will and won't say reflects the rules of the market it was built for.
